note: The shared case table for the word-alphabet refusal of §8.2. Both stacks read THIS file: `fragmented_words` (llm_geometry/arch/vacancy_score.py) and `fragmentedWords` (src/lib/staticClient/byteSpans.ts) must return `fragmented` exactly, in order. A case is here because it names a rule, not because it is an example — see `why`.

cases.text: the cat sat on the mat
cases.why: plain ASCII: nothing is fragmented, so nothing is refused
WORD_RE's own apostrophe: it matches the run entirely
WORD_RE's own hyphen: it matches the run entirely
U+2019, the apostrophe every smart-quotes editor emits. Scored 200 and swapped to 'big’t' before the joiner class existed
U+203F undertie, general category Pc. Pc was missing from BOTH stacks until 2026-08-04: this scored 200 and swapped to 'warm‿t'
U+005F low line, the commonest Pc there is
U+FF3F fullwidth low line — Pc reached through the fullwidth forms
U+FE4D dashed low line — Pc reached through the presentation forms

U+0890 is genuinely Cf, but only from Unicode 14. Python 3.10 carries Unicode 13.0 and used to call it unassigned, so the backend scored this and swapped it to 'warm࢐t' while the browser refused it. The pinned table is why both now refuse
U+2E5D oblique hyphen — Pd from Unicode 14, the same skew on the dash half of the class
U+10D6E is Pd from Unicode 16 and is ASTRAL — it also pins that the run scanner works in code points, not UTF-16 units
U+00AD soft hyphen: invisible, so a reader cannot see why the score would be wrong
U+200D zero-width joiner: invisible, same class
U+061C Arabic letter mark — Cf both runtimes have always known, so this stays green even if the pin moves
U+2010 hyphen — Pd, and NOT the ASCII hyphen WORD_RE accepts
U+05F3 Hebrew geresh — a named joiner: category Po, indistinguishable from a quotation mark by property alone
U+00B7 middle dot, the Catalan l·l — another named joiner
the LETTER half of the alphabet: WORD_RE sees 'caf', and 'a café' vacated to 'a washé'
the letter half again, and the shape that produced a 500 rather than a wrong number
combining acute on 'r' has no precomposed form, so NFC does not remove it; a mark belongs to the letter it sits on, so this is one run

the Gutenberg em-dash convention, present in this project's own corpus. Written entirely in WORD_RE's alphabet, so refusing it offered the reader no way to comply. Each piece is a whole ASCII word the transform vacates AS a word
the other three real instances from the corpus, in one passage
the apostrophe half of the same rule: a doubled ASCII apostrophe is still WORD_RE's own alphabet
a RUN of joiners still joins when the joiners are not WORD_RE's own — the ASCII escape hatch above must not become a hole for repeated invisible characters
a joiner with no letter after it is punctuation, not a joiner: the run ends at 'don'
the same rule for the ASCII hyphen used as a dash between words
runs WORD_RE never touches are not fragmented: they are never vacated, are byte-identical in all three variants, and are attributed to no word
